name: seq
readme:
Short:        Print sequences of numbers
Type:         util/cli
Architecture: m68k-amigaos >= 3.0
Uploader:     duncan (at) bowring (dot) us
Author:       Todd C. Miller (ported by Duncan Bowring)
Version:      1.8

seq - Print sequences of numbers

Original author: Todd C. Miller
Source: OpenBSD seq v1.8

Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in FS-UAE with AmigaOS 3.1.

Usage:
  seq [-w] [-f format] [-s string] [-t string] [first [incr]] last

Options:
  -w          Equalize widths with leading zeros
  -f format   printf-style format for numbers
  -s string   Separator (default: newline)
  -t string   Terminator (default: newline)

Includes full source code (original OpenBSD and ported Amiga versions)
and PORT.md documenting every transformation applied.
porting_notes: Requires libm (-lm) for math functions. Uses amiport_asprintf() for dynamic format string building. Stack cookie set to 8192 bytes (sufficient for printf/snprintf headroom). 47 tests cover all flags (-w, -f, -s, -t), integer and floating-point sequences, descending sequences, error paths (zero increment, wrong direction, invalid format specifiers), edge cases (first==last, unreachable endpoint), and real-world Amiga usage patterns. Memory-checker: CLEAN. Perf-optimizer: CLEAN.
